title: Standardised and extended trading hours (Queensland)
summary: The Trading (Allowable Hours) Amendment Act 2017 replaced the trading hours order with statutory hours: in south-east Queensland non-exempt shops may open 7am-9pm Monday-Saturday and 9am-6pm Sundays and public holidays.

commenced.what: Act commenced; 2017 trading hours order repealed

direction_rationale: Longer permitted trading hours let smaller and new retailers compete with incumbents on convenience and give consumers more choice; the PC recommended full deregulation. Effects may favour large chains able to staff extra hours.
comparison: Other restricted states (SA); regional vs SEQ Queensland
notes: Part of the change formalised a 2016 QIRC decision; independent retailers remain exempt.

verified.notes: Assent date not confirmed; commencement from QIRC trading hours order document.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 14-15 October 2026 from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Replaced Queensland's trading hours orders with statutory hours: in south-east Queensland, shops may open 7am to 9pm Monday to Saturday and on Sundays. Longer, simpler hours let shops compete on convenience.

marks.reason: Longer permitted hours let retailers compete on convenience.
Simple statutory hours replace a complex set of trading hours orders.
